To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the participation layer can be used in a multiplex community detection setting and that it can be used to identify communities that are more relevant than those obtained from the interaction layer alone.

the use of participation data in addition to interaction data leads to more stable communities, that the communities found with this data are more relevant in the political context and that the communities found are more stable than communities found only using explicit interaction data.

(1) we propose a novel data layer for multiplex community detection that is based on the participation of users in a hashtag, and (2) we show that this participation data can be used to detect communities in Twitter data that differ from those found by using only the explicit interaction data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new data source for social media analysis and its application to a specific domain, namely political communication on Twitter.
the following two aspects.
the following question: How to detect communities in online social media by taking into account the participation of users in discussions about a specific topic?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of interaction data for community detection in online media can be improved by considering the participation data layer as well.
the use of interaction data alone can result in a biased view of social media communities, while the inclusion of the additional layer of participation data can provide an important complement.
the data layer of user participation can be used to detect communities in social media that are not necessarily found in the layer of user interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data about the interaction between the users is not sufficient for community detection, but the data about the participation of the users is sufficient for community detection.
we are trying to understand the role of the imagined audience in the context of social media and how to use it to find communities.

we are able to detect different types of communities by using a novel method to construct a participation layer from Twitter data and applying multiplex network community detection algorithms to the combined interaction and participation layers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data about user participation is crucial for community detection, especially for multiplex community detection in the case of political communication.

the data used for community detection in social media should include the invisible audiences that users are targeting with their messages, as they are a fundamental part of the participatory behavior that is the basis of social media.
the interaction data provided by the social media platform is only one of many possible sources of information about the social structure of an online community.
